battle.name: 陳橋兵變
battle.brief: 顯德七年正月初四，後周北征大軍行至汴京六十里外的陳橋驛，宿營而黃旗已起。殿前都點檢趙匡胤被軍士以黃袍加身，諸將羅拜，回師入汴，迫恭帝退位，北宋開國。此役不聞一矢之發，卻終結了五代十國的藩鎮割據，開出重文輕武的格局。卡面羅馬弩砲並未隨軍而至，其後裔床弩與砲車是北宋禁軍的攻城骨幹。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 陳橋兵變並非兩國交兵，而是後周朝廷與自家禁軍之間的一次授權轉移，所以要把它當作交戰方來看，只能分內外兩個層次。外層是後周所面對的敵境：北漢據太原，契丹即遼雄踞北方，顯德六年冬世宗北伐受挫，河朔與山東邊防空虛，顯德七年正月北漢與遼的入寇消息同時傳到汴京，朝廷於是調諸道兵北上，殿前都點檢趙匡胤受命為北征統帥，率宿禁軍出師。內層是汴京城內的權力結構：後周承唐末五代之制，樞密院掌軍令而以文官為主，殿前司、侍衛馬軍司、侍衛步軍司合稱三衙，掌禁軍宿衛與出征；兵權一分為二，樞密使調兵而三衙統兵，節度使仍鎮一方、握一州財賦，禁軍與藩鎮並存，禁軍是《宋史·兵志》所說天下精銳、四方讖服的正軍，禁軍將士多取自河北、山南、西蜀強壯之家，糧餉厚給，與地方蕃兵分離，士卒的忠誠因此更多繫於京師統帥一身。陳橋當夜，奪旗與擁立的一方是趙匡胤的宿衛集團，包括石守信、高懷德、張令徽等禁軍宿將；被奪的一方是後周幼主郭宗訓與其母符氏所居的宮廷，以及握著樞密院印信的文官班子，名義上他們仍是正統，實際上已無兵可用。城外的北漢與契丹在整件事中並未參與，陳橋之後數年，遼廷也沒有趁新朝初立而大舉南侵，這是北宋得以在二十年內完成統一的重要外部條件。
countriesEn: Chenqiao was not a war between two states but a transfer of authorisation between the Later Zhou court and its own imperial guard, and so the two sides can only be set out in an outer and an inner layer. The outer layer is the hostile world the Later Zhou faced: Northern Han held Taiyuan and the Khitan, that is the Liao, dominated the north; after the winter of 959, when the emperor's northern campaign had gone wrong, the frontier in Hebei and in Shandong lay thin, and in the first month of 960 the reports of incursions by Northern Han and the Liao reached Bianjing at the same time. The court therefore mustered troops from the circuits to march north, and Zhao Kuangyin, commander of the palace troops, was appointed to lead that expedition with the guard that slept in the palace. The inner layer is the structure of power inside the capital. The Later Zhou inherited the institutions of the late Tang and of the Five Dynasties: the Privy Council issued the military orders under civil officials, while the Palace Troops Office, the Mounted Guards Office and the Foot Guards Office, together called the Three Commands, held the imperial guard and the field forces. Military authority was split in two, the Council commanding on paper and the Three Commands commanding in fact, while the provincial governors still sat upon their circuits with the revenues of a prefecture in their hands. The standing guard and the provincial forces existed side by side, and the guard was what the History of Song in its treatise on arms calls the elite of the realm, obeyed throughout the four quarters; its soldiers were taken from the strong families of Hebei, of Shan'nan and of western Shu, paid generously, and separated from the provincial levies, so that the loyalty of the men attached itself less to the dynasty than to the commander at the capital. On the night at Chenqiao the side that seized the standard and made the acclamation was Zhao Kuangyin's own guard group, with such seasoned soldiers of the guard as Shi Shouxin, Gao Huaide and Zhang Linghui; the side that was dispossessed was the court of the child emperor Guo Zongxun, the palace of the empress dowager Fu, and the civil officials holding the seals of the Privy Council, who remained the legitimate authority in name but had no troops with which to enforce anything. Neither Northern Han nor the Liao took part in any of it, and for several years after Chenqiao the Liao court did not launch a great southern war against the new dynasty; that was the external condition that allowed the Northern Song to complete its unification within twenty years.
people: 史冊留下姓名的，多數屬於擁立的一方。趙匡胤生於927年卒於976年，字德昌，趙州涿郡人，父趙弘殷歷仕後唐後晉，出身軍人世家，他自己也是禁軍出身：從羅成隊將、殿前侍衛、殿前都指揮使一路做到殿前都點檢，掌著貼近皇帝的宿衛精兵。關鍵的一場仗是954年的高平之戰，後周世宗柴榮親征北漢，樊愛能率遼騎萬餘追奔，投河死者甚眾，柴榮怒而斬樊愛能等七十餘人，趙匡胤卻在陣中生擒樊愛能，這一筆奠定了他在禁軍中的地位。另一個關鍵人物是趙普，生於922年卒於992年，華州趙氏，後為趙匡胤幕僚；陳橋事起，他星夜追至軍中，眾將問計，他說天命已有所歸，宜即大位；事後他為宰相，主持收兵權、削藩鎮，後人以半部論語治天下之說稱之。禁軍宿將石守信與趙匡胤同宿多年，陳橋之夜推舉最力；趙匡胤之妹夫高懷德同為骨幹；張令徽、張德欽亦參與其事。宮廷那邊的主人後周恭帝郭宗訓，生於953年，顯德六年十月以六歲登基，其母出自吳越符氏，宦官與外戚在幼主周圍形成屏障，卻調不動禁軍。柴榮生於921年卒於959年，雖已崩逝，他的布置仍在：正是他提拔趙匡胤掌禁軍、宿衛左右，故老將宿將普遍以周室名器為號召。趙匡胤之弟趙光義時任禁軍要職，事變當夜已在汴京，隨後以守內之任參預其成；另一名幕僚李崇矩與內侍一班人則在城內接應，汴京禁軍響應，兵不血刃地完成了城內的交接。
peopleEn: The names that survive in the histories belong mostly to the side that made the acclamation. Zhao Kuangyin, born in 927 and dead in 976, courtesy name Dechang, was a native of Zhuojun in Zhaozhou; his father Zhao Hongyin had served the Later Tang and the Later Jin, and the family was a military one, and he too came up through the guard, from a captain of the Luocheng company and a palace guard and commander of the palace troops up to commander of the palace troops, the officer who held the elite body quartering close to the emperor. The decisive engagement in his career was the battle of Gaoping in 954, when the Later Zhou emperor Chai Rong marched in person against Northern Han and Fan Aineng led more than ten thousand Liao horsemen in the pursuit, with many of them drowned in the river; the emperor in his anger executed Fan Aineng and more than seventy others, while Zhao Kuangyin took Fan Aineng alive on the field, and that deed settled his standing in the guard. The other key figure was Zhao Pu, born in 922 and dead in 992, a man of the Zhao clan of Huazhou who became Zhao Kuangyin's adviser; when the business at Chenqiao broke out he rode after the army through the night, and when the generals asked him for a plan he said that the mandate of Heaven had already declared its choice and that they ought to take the great position at once. He afterwards became chancellor and directed the taking of the troops back and the reduction of the provincial governors, and later ages spoke of ruling the realm with half a copy of the Analects. Shi Shouxin, a seasoned soldier of the guard who had long slept in the palace alongside Zhao Kuangyin, pushed hardest for the acclamation on the night at Chenqiao; Gao Huaide, the brother-in-law of Zhao Kuangyin through his sister, was another of the core; Zhang Linghui and Zhang Deqin took part as well. On the other side stood the child emperor of the Later Zhou, Guo Zongxun, born in 953, who had been enthroned in the tenth month of 959 at the age of six, his mother the empress Fu being of the Fu clan of Wuyue; eunuchs and maternal relatives formed a screen around the child, and yet they could not move the guard. Chai Rong, born in 921 and dead in 959, had been dead for some time, but his arrangements were still in force: it was he who had raised Zhao Kuangyin to command the guard and to sleep at the emperor's side, and so the old generals gave their obedience in the name of the Zhou house. Zhao Kuangyin's younger brother Zhao Guangyi held an important post in the guard and was already in Bianjing on the night of the business, and afterwards took part in carrying it through as the man who held the inside; another adviser, Li Chongju, and a group of palace servants made the reception inside the city, the guard of Bianjing answering the call, and the handover within the walls was accomplished without a drop of blood.
kits: 先說清楚一件事：卡面上這具羅馬弩砲並沒有出現在陳橋。陳橋兵變全無攻城之戰，弩砲一類的攻城與守城重器當時不在這條驛道上；卡面講它拆掉希臘的城牆，更準確地說，是它在圍城中以標槍射斃城頭守軍、切斷城防與街市之間的聯絡，讓城牆失去作用，而在中國，這條血緣延續下來的就是弩砲。羅馬弩砲是扭力絞盤發射的單發標槍機，一發一具箭：槍身用細長的杉木或白蠍木，外裹麻布與皮條，操作要先以腳踏或絞盤上弦，一具機需數人合力發射，標槍重約一公斤，射程可及數百步。中國與之最接近的裝備是床弩與車弩：床弩架在木床上，用槓桿或絞盤張弦，一發一具大矢，需三五人操作，備矢數十；車弩則把弩機安在車上，隨軍移動。床弩的記載在唐代已見於兵書《太白陰經》，北宋崇寧年間成書的《武經總要》又把弩與砲各十一種的形制、備件、用法繪成圖樣，把散用千年的器械標準化。與弩砲同時代、也在宋軍編制內的攻城器械還有：配重式與槓桿式拋石機，宋人稱砲；雲梯車與飛雲梯；撞車；拒馬與鹿角；壕車與雉堞；掘地所用的地道與壅塞的坑道。燃燒類武器則有火矢、以猛火油灌入的拒馬槍與投擲的火球，960年時火藥仍以硫黃為主，尚未成為攻城的主兵器。防具上，禁軍用皮甲、札甲與部分藤甲，鎗、矛、刀、弓箭並用，橫刀與桿刀是主力；後勤靠驢騾輜重、牛車與汴河漕運。總之，弩砲在這場政變裡沒有上陣的機會，它在這裡的意義是技術譜系的一個座標：宋代那些把石頭送出城、把標槍壓向城頭的器械，與它隔著一千年的時空，卻共享同一條設計原理。
kitsEn: One thing must be said first: the Roman scorpio on the card did not appear at Chenqiao. The coup involved no siege at all, and heavy machines of the scorpio and siege kind were not on that post road. The card says the Romans used it to break down the walls of the Greek cities; more precisely, it was used in the siege to shoot the defenders on the ramparts with heavy bolts, to cut the link between the defences and the streets, and so to make the wall useless. In China the line of descent from that machine is the crossbow artillery. The Roman scorpio was a single-shot bolt-thrower worked by torsion from a windlass, one bolt to the machine: the bolt shaft was of slender fir or white heartwood, bound round with hemp cloth and leather, the cord had to be wound up with the feet or by a windlass before firing, several men were needed to loose one machine, the bolt weighed about a kilogramme, and its reach ran to several hundred paces. The closest Chinese equivalents were the bed crossbow and the cart crossbow. The bed crossbow stood on a wooden bed, was drawn with a lever or a windlass, loosed one heavy bolt at a time, needed three to five men to work and carried several dozen bolts; the cart crossbow had its mechanism mounted on a wagon so that it could move with the column. The bed crossbow is already recorded in the Tang military manual the Taibai Yin Jing, and the Wujing Zongyao, completed in the Chongning era of the Northern Song, set out in drawings the forms, the fittings and the employment of eleven kinds of crossbow and eleven kinds of stone-throwing machine, standardising instruments that had been used in scattered fashion for a thousand years. Contemporary with the scorpio and also in the Song order of battle were the siege engines: counterweight and beam stone-throwers, which the Chinese called the pao; cloud-ladder carts and flying cloud ladders; battering rams; cheval-de-frise and antler-shaped barriers; trench carts and rampart screens; and the underground galleries and choke trenches dug by sappers. The burning weapons included fire arrows, cheval-de-frise spears filled with oil, and thrown fire balls; in 960 gunpowder was still essentially sulphur and had not yet become the main siege charge. On protection, the guard wore hide armour, plated armour and some rattan armour, and used spear, halberd, sword and bow, the straight sword and the pole sword being the core; supply rested on mule and donkey trains, ox carts and the Bian canal. In sum, the scorpio had no opportunity to fight in this coup. Its significance here is that of a coordinate on a technical genealogy: the Song instruments that flung stones out of a city and pressed bolts against a rampart stand a thousand years away from it in time, yet share the same principle of design.
tactics: 陳橋兵變沒有戰鬥，但有清楚的戰術邏輯，而且這套邏輯全在授權與接管上。第一步是把名分做熟：顯德七年正月朝廷議北征，趙匡胤以殿前都點檢兼北征統帥出師，宿衛將士隨行，這支部隊在出京前已是他的人馬。出征途中大軍宿營，據說軍紀寬弛，趙匡胤不嚴禁士卒就食於州縣，軍心更見渙散，也有人說這是他有意縱之，以為亂鋪墊。第二步是製造天命的現場：夜宿陳橋，軍中先有黃旗出沒，人皆以為非常之兆；隨後有人把黃袍披上趙匡胤身上，他推辭再三，諸將羅拜請即大位，於是眾心遂定，這一步的目的不是選舉，而是把已經存在的軍事優勢轉換成不可反悔的名分。第三步是入城：趙匡胤即將回師，先遣人告變，汴京城內的禁軍與侍衛在石守信等宿將率領下響應，張永德等與他同掌禁軍的老將交出宿衛之權，城門自開，全城沒有交鋒。第四步是程序上的合法化：先遣翰林學士陶毅奉恭帝之詔往迎，然後由趙匡胤入城建隆元年、大赦、改元，把兵變套進禪代的舊格式裡。第五步是善後與收編：入城後厚待宿將、給予厚賞，安置符氏與幼主，遣散各路援軍回鎮，接著逐年把精兵收歸禁軍、以文臣出守州郡，把政變的成果轉成制度。整個過程的關鍵是速度：從披袍到即位只隔一夜，從陳橋到汴梁不過數日，因為禁軍的忠誠已在多年宿衛中集中到一人身上，任何拖延都會讓別人搶先動手，同樣的兵變但由別人發動，結局可能相反。糧秣方面，大軍正月出征靠汴河與沿線州縣供應，汴京一帶冬儲有限，宿營待旦、就地取給是當時的常態。
tacticsEn: There was no fighting at Chenqiao, but there is a clear tactical logic, and the whole of it lies in authorisation and in taking over. The first step was to make the forms of legitimacy familiar. In the first month of 960 the court debated the northern expedition, and Zhao Kuangyin marched out as commander of the palace troops and commander of that expedition, the sleeping guard going with him; before the column left the capital it was already his men. On the march the army encamped, and it is said that discipline was loose, that Zhao Kuangyin did not rigorously forbid the soldiers from taking their food from the prefectures on the way, and that the morale of the men grew still more slack; some hold that he let it happen on purpose, laying the ground for disorder. The second step was to stage the omen of Heaven. The army lay at Chenqiao by night, yellow banners were seen among the camp first, and all took it for a sign out of the ordinary; then someone draped the yellow robe over Zhao Kuangyin, he declined again and again, the generals bowed themselves in a circle and begged him to take the great position, and so the hearts of the men were settled. The purpose of that step was not an election but the conversion of a military advantage already held into a title that could not be taken back. The third step was the entry into the city. As Zhao Kuangyin was about to march back, he sent word ahead; the guard and the palace troops inside Bianjing answered under such seasoned soldiers as Shi Shouxin, old generals such as Zhang Yongde who had shared command of the guard with him handed over the duty of the inner quarters, the gates opened of themselves, and there was no fighting anywhere in the city. The fourth step was the legalising of the procedure: a Hanlin scholar, Tao Yi, was first sent to meet the emperor with the edict of the child emperor Guo Zongxun, and then Zhao Kuangyin entered the city, established the era Jianlong, issued a general pardon and changed the year, fitting the mutiny into the old mould of an abdication. The fifth step was the settling of accounts and the taking over of the men. After entering the city he treated the seasoned soldiers generously, rewarded them handsomely, settled the empress Fu and the child prince, dispersed the reinforcing armies back to their circuits, and then year by year drew the elite troops back into the guard and sent civil officials to govern the prefectures, converting the results of the coup into institutions. The key to the whole process was speed: from the robe to the acceptance of the throne took a single night, and from Chenqiao to Bianjing only a few days, because the loyalty of the guard had been concentrated on one man through years of service in the palace, and any delay would have allowed somebody else to strike first; the same mutiny begun by a different man might have ended differently. On supply, the army that marched in the first month drew provisions from the Bian canal and from the prefectures along the route; the winter stores around the capital were thin, and halting overnight and taking food from the country was the normal practice of the time.
data: 可核對的數字分四類。第一類是文獻自述的日期與地點：事變在後周顯德七年正月初四，即960年，地點是汴京正北約六十里、合今三十公里上下的陳橋驛，今屬河南封丘縣陳橋鎮一帶；趙匡胤即位時實歲三十三、虛歲三十四，生於927年，卒於976年；柴榮生於921年，卒於959年；恭帝郭宗訓生於953年，即位時年僅六歲。第二類是與陳橋直接相關的編制與人數：據《宋史·兵志》所載各期置兵額推算，宋初禁軍總額在二十萬上下，其中騎兵約六萬餘、步兵約十餘萬，而地方節度使所領蕃兵尚不下數十萬；同書以天下精銳、四方讖服形容禁軍，說明這支部隊的規模與榮耀都遠超前朝。兵變的直接參與者人數並不多，說得清楚名字的是石守信、高懷德、張令徽、張德欽等禁軍宿將，加上城內接應的一批內侍與侍衛，事前的確切人數史書並無記載。第三類是作戰史上的對照數：954年的高平之戰是五代中少見的大會戰，世宗親征北漢，樊愛能率遼騎萬餘追奔，柴榮斬樊愛能等七十餘人，趙匡胤生擒樊愛能；顯德六年世宗北伐，奪瀛州莫州而不能久守，南征南唐則三戰三捷、克壽州，這幾場勝仗把禁軍的戰鬥力推到頂點，也把誰能帶這支部隊的問題推到台前。第四類是時距與後果：五代自907年朱溫代唐到960年，前後五十三年；陳橋之後，北宋用二十年完成統一，963年下荊南，964年滅後蜀，975年滅南唐，979年吳越納土、北漢國亡。歷時、兵力、戰果與疆域變化都可與正史紀年對照，不必臆造精確傷亡，陳橋兵變本身沒有戰鬥，也就沒有傷亡可數。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into four classes. The first class is what the documents say of the date and the place. The mutiny came on the fourth day of the first month of the seventh year of Xian De of the Later Zhou, that is 960, at the post station of Chenqiao about sixty li, some thirty kilometres in the modern measure, due north of Bianjing, in what is now the township of Chenqiao in Fengqiu county, Henan. Zhao Kuangyin was thirty-three by western count, thirty-four by Chinese count, at his accession; he was born in 927 and died in 976. Chai Rong was born in 921 and died in 959. The child emperor Guo Zongxun was born in 953 and was six years old at his enthronement. The second class concerns the order of battle and the numbers directly involved at Chenqiao. Working out from the establishment figures for the various periods recorded in the History of Song in its treatise on arms, the total strength of the guard in the early Northern Song was on the order of two hundred thousand, of which perhaps sixty-odd thousand were cavalry and something over a hundred thousand foot, while the provincial forces still held by the circuit governors numbered no fewer than several hundred thousand. The same work describes the guard as the elite of the realm obeyed throughout the four quarters, which shows that the size and the standing of this army exceeded anything known in the preceding dynasties. The number of men directly engaged in the mutiny was small: the names that can be given are the seasoned soldiers of the guard such as Shi Shouxin, Gao Huaide, Zhang Linghui and Zhang Deqin, together with a group of palace servants and attendants who made the reception inside the walls, and no exact figure for the numbers concerned survives in the histories. The third class is the comparative record of actual fighting. The battle of Gaoping in 954 was one of the few great set-piece battles of the Five Dynasties: the emperor marched in person against Northern Han, Fan Aineng led more than ten thousand Liao horsemen in the pursuit, the emperor executed Fan Aineng and more than seventy others, and Zhao Kuangyin took Fan Aineng alive. In 959 the emperor campaigned north, took Yuzhou and Mozhou but could not hold them, and campaigning south against Southern Tang he won three engagements in succession and took Shouchou. Those victories pushed the fighting quality of the guard to its height and at the same time drove to the front the question of who should command that army. The fourth class is the interval and the consequences. The Five Dynasties lasted fifty-three years, from Zhu Wen's usurpation of the Tang in 907 to 960. After Chenqiao the Northern Song took twenty years to unify: Jingnan fell in 963, Later Shu in 964, Southern Tang in 975, and in 979 Wuyue surrendered its territory and Northern Han ceased to exist. Duration, strength, results and the change of territory can all be checked against the annals; there is no need to invent precise casualty figures, and Chenqiao involved no fighting, so there are no casualties to count.
cause: 打起來的直接起因是後周最高權力的突然真空。顯德六年六月，世宗柴榮在北伐回師後病逝，臨終把禁軍宿衛與殿前司交到趙匡胤手裡；十月，六歲的郭宗訓即位，樞密院由文官主持、殿前司由武將主持，兩套系統彼此防範，而禁軍成了唯一能直接決定誰做皇帝的力量，這支部隊的效忠對象並非宮中的幼主，而是多年宿衛在皇帝左右的趙匡胤。深層原因是五代留下的制度病竈：方鎮擁兵自重雖然已被削平，禁軍卻過度膨脹，節度使仍掌一州之財，樞密院與三衙互相牽制，任何一環出問題都會震動整個局面。趙普的勸進是政治現實的計算：禁軍不可能沒有統帥，幼主無法駕馭這支部隊，換一個人接管只會再演一次兵變，與其讓不可預知的人兵變，不如由這支部隊最信任、也最能服眾的那一位來完成。外部條件同樣重要：顯德七年正月北漢與契丹的入寇消息逼出北征這道命令，名義上是一次保衛國家的軍事行動，實際上把趙匡胤和禁軍帶離汴京城，放在一條回得去也退不得的路上；士卒久戍，行伍無紀，禁令一旦鬆動，軍心就會向著能給他們新秩序的人傾斜。於是有了陳橋之夜：那不是反叛朝廷，而是軍隊把已經握在手中的武力，兌換成一份名分。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the affair was the sudden vacuum at the top of the Later Zhou. In the sixth month of 959 the emperor Chai Rong fell ill after the northern campaign and died, and on his deathbed he left the guard and the palace troops office in the hands of Zhao Kuangyin. In the tenth month the six-year-old Guo Zongxun was enthroned; the Privy Council was run by civil officials and the palace troops office by soldiers, the two systems were set to watch one another, and the guard had become the only force that could decide directly who would be emperor. The allegiance of that force did not rest with the child in the palace but with Zhao Kuangyin, who had slept in the palace at the emperor's side for years. The deeper cause lay in the institutional lesions left by the Five Dynasties. The autonomous power of the provincial governors had been broken, but the guard had grown out of all proportion, the circuit governors still held the revenues of their prefectures, and the Privy Council and the Three Commands cancelled one another out; a failure in any one of these would shake the whole structure. The counsel of Zhao Pu was an exercise in political realism. The guard could not be without a commander; a child could not hold it; handing it to some other man would only produce another mutiny; and rather than let an unpredictable man mutiny, it was better that the one the army trusted, and the one best able to hold the men together, should do it. The external conditions mattered just as much. The reports of incursions by Northern Han and the Liao in the first month of 960 forced out the order for the northern expedition, which in name was a measure to defend the state, and in fact took Zhao Kuangyin and the guard out of Bianjing and set them on a road from which they could go forward but not back. Men long in the field, an army without discipline, the loosening of a single prohibition, and the hearts of the soldiers turned towards the man who could give them a new order. That is how the night at Chenqiao came about: it was not a rebellion against the court, but the army converting military force it already held into a title.
impact: 陳橋兵變開啟的，是中國歷史上一段以集權而非兼併為特徵的時期。第一，它終結了五代：自907年朱溫代唐到960年，前後五十三年的政權更替多伴隨流血，陳橋之後的開端卻是安寧的，建隆元年趙匡胤大赦、減稅、釋囚，962年就平掉了最早發難的潞王之變，此後十餘年間荊南、後蜀、南唐、吳越、北漢相繼覆亡或納土，979年海內歸於一統。第二，它建立了北宋的兵制骨架：收精兵，把地方上的強銳調入禁軍，禁軍成為全國唯一的常備精銳；削實權，節度使逐步只剩虛銜，州郡由文臣知州、通判監稅；制錢谷，財權歸於中央；兵權分屬三衙與樞密院，文武相制；並行更戍之法，使將不專兵、兵不識將，日後的杯酒釋兵權即在此一脈之上。第三，它扭轉了歷來的政策重心：武人兵變奪位曾經是常事，陳橋之後皇帝出自禁軍宿衛而非藩鎮，朝廷必須以文官、科舉與制度約束武人，重文輕武由此成為北宋的基本國策，長期的和平與文化繁盛由此而來，邊疆則長期處於守勢，兩者同出一源。第四，它在文獻與地景上都留下了痕跡：陳橋驛至今有宋太祖黃袍加身處的石碑與祠祀，開封城內的舊營區地名仍可與《東京夢華錄》對照，而陳橋兵變與杯酒釋兵權都成了漢語裡固定的成語，成為後人談論權力交接的現成範例。
impactEn: What Chenqiao opened was a period of Chinese history characterised by centralisation rather than by annexation. First, it ended the Five Dynasties. From Zhu Wen's usurpation of the Tang in 907 to 960, fifty-three years of dynastic turnover were accompanied by bloodshed; the beginning after Chenqiao was peaceful, for in the first year of Jianlong Zhao Kuangyin issued a general pardon, reduced taxes and released prisoners, and in 962 he put down the revolt of the Prince of Lu, the first rising of his reign; within the following ten years or so Jingnan, Later Shu, Southern Tang, Wuyue and Northern Han were destroyed or surrendered their territory, and by 979 the realm was unified. Second, it built the skeleton of the Northern Song military system: gathering the elite troops, so that the guard became the only standing elite force in the realm; stripping the provincial governors of real power, until the circuit governors kept nothing but an empty title, the prefectures being governed by civil officials with a sub-prefectural controller over the taxes; bringing the revenues to the centre; dividing military authority between the Three Commands and the Privy Council so that civil and military checked one another; and instituting the rotation of troops, so that a general did not hold his men and the men did not know their general. The famous drinking of the cup that stripped the veterans of their commands grew out of this same line. Third, it turned the whole policy of the age around. For a soldier to seize the throne by mutiny had been commonplace; after Chenqiao the emperor came from the guard rather than from a provincial governor, and the court had to hold the military men in check with civil officials, examinations and institutions. The primacy of civil over military became the basic policy of the Northern Song, and the long peace and cultural flowering came from it, while the frontier remained on the defensive for the same reason. Fourth, it left traces in the documents and in the landscape: at Chenqiao post station there are still a stele and a shrine marking the place where the yellow robe was placed on Song Taizu, the old barrack names inside Kaifeng can still be checked against the Record of the Capital of the Eastern Capital, and both Chenqiao and the cup that stripped the veterans of command have become fixed expressions in the language and ready-made examples for later talk about the transfer of power.
result: 顯德七年正月初四夜，陳橋驛的營中，黃袍披上趙匡胤的肩，諸將羅拜，請即大位；他辭讓再三，直到眾心堅定才受命。次日大軍整旅而還，汴京城內的禁軍與侍衛同時響應，宿將交出宿衛，城門自開，趙匡胤入城，奉後周恭帝退位，大赦天下，改元建隆，後周亡，北宋立。整件事沒有交戰，沒有攻城，血未曾流在陳橋的驛道上，所以後世稱之為不流血之變。結果可以分三層看：政權層面，一個延續了半個世紀的割據局面以一次政變收束，北宋的江山自此開始；制度層面，趙匡胤在接下來的十一年裡把陳橋的一夜變成一套制度，收精兵、削實權、制錢谷、分兵權、罷宿將，完成了五代想做而沒有做成的事；長遠層面，陳橋兵變也定下了此後三百年天子的心理範式，皇帝由禁軍的信任推舉而成，因此既要防備禁軍，也要防備推舉禁軍的那些人。它留下的問題同樣清楚：一個靠軍隊授權建立的王朝，終究要回答如何安頓這支部隊。答案用了二十年的統一和上百年的重文政策才慢慢寫完，而其中最著名的一筆，寫在開寶年間那場只有一杯酒的酒席上。
resultEn: On the night of the fourth day of the first month of the seventh year of Xian De, in the camp at the post station of Chenqiao, the yellow robe was laid on Zhao Kuangyin's shoulders, the generals bowed themselves in a circle and begged him to take the great position; he declined again and again and only accepted when the hearts of the men were settled. The next day the army marched back in good order, the guard and the palace troops inside Bianjing answered at the same moment, the veterans handed over the inner quarters, the gates opened of themselves, and Zhao Kuangyin entered the city, received the abdication of the child emperor of the Later Zhou, issued a general pardon and changed the year to Jianlong. The Later Zhou ceased to exist and the Northern Song began. There was no engagement, no siege, and no blood was spilled on the post road at Chenqiao, which is why later ages have called it a change of dynasty without bloodshed. The result can be read on three levels. At the level of power, a situation of partition that had run for half a century was wound up in a single mutiny, and from that moment the realm of the Northern Song began. At the level of institutions, over the eleven years that followed Zhao Kuangyin turned the single night of Chenqiao into a system, gathering the elite troops, stripping the governors of real power, taking the revenues to the centre, dividing military authority and retiring the veterans, and so accomplished what the Five Dynasties had wanted to do and had not managed. In the long run, Chenqiao also fixed the psychology of the emperors of the three centuries that followed: the sovereign was raised by the trust of the guard, and so the court had to guard against the guard and against those who would raise the guard. The question it left behind is equally clear. A dynasty founded on the authorisation of an army must in the end answer the question of how to settle that army, and the answer took twenty years of unification and a hundred years of civil policy to write out slowly, the most famous stroke of it being written at the table with a single cup of wine in the Kaibao years.
